453	    async def _reconcile_protective_on_exit(
454	        self, trader_id: str, occ_symbol: str, remaining: int
455	    ) -> None:
456	        """The trader's manual SELL/TRIM takes precedence over the automated stop/target:
457	        make the contract's working protective legs cover exactly `remaining` contracts
458	        (0 on a full exit). Stop and take-profit are reconciled independently — each should
459	        cover `remaining`; within a type, distribute oldest-first, cancelling the excess and
460	        shrinking the one leg that straddles the boundary, so total coverage never exceeds
461	        what's held (no resurrected oversell)."""
462	        legs = await ostore.working_protective_for_contract(self.conn, trader_id, occ_symbol)
463	        by_type: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
464	        for leg in legs:
465	            by_type.setdefault(leg["signal_type"], []).append(leg)
466	        for group in by_type.values():
467	            left = remaining
468	            for leg in group:  # already oldest-first from the query
469	                ref = ostore.order_ref(trader_id, leg["order_id"])
470	                covered = int(leg["requested_qty"]) - int(leg["filled_qty"] or 0)
471	                keep = max(0, min(covered, left))
472	                if keep <= 0:
473	                    await self.ib.cancel(ref)
474	                    await ostore.update_order(
475	                        self.conn, leg["order_id"], status=ostore.CANCELLED)
476	                elif keep < covered:
477	                    new_total = int(leg["filled_qty"] or 0) + keep
478	                    await self.ib.modify(ref, qty=new_total)
479	                    await ostore.update_order(
480	                        self.conn, leg["order_id"], requested_qty=new_total)
481	                left -= keep

483	    # ---- placement + persistence + notifications -----------------------
484	    async def _place_and_record(
485	        self, signal, occ, side, qty, contract, limit_price,
486	        protective: ProtectiveExit | None = None,
487	    ) -> None:
488	        # Order type follows the signal: a stated price → limit at that price (± spread,
489	        # already baked into limit_price); no price → market.
490	        order_type = "limit" if limit_price is not None else "market"
491	        sent_limit = limit_price
492	        con_id = getattr(contract, "conId", None)
493	        log.info(
494	            "Placing %s %s %dx %s @ %s", order_type, side, qty, occ,
495	            f"{sent_limit:g}" if sent_limit is not None else "market",
496	        )
497	
498	        order_id = await ostore.create_order(
499	            self.conn, signal=signal, occ_symbol=occ, requested_qty=qty,
500	            limit_price=sent_limit, con_id=con_id, status=ostore.PENDING,
501	        )
502	        await self._notify_placed(signal, side, qty, sent_limit, order_id)
503	
504	        # Record the protective-exit legs as their own PENDING SELL rows so their later
505	        # fills/cancellations reconcile back via the order-update callback (keyed by ref).
506	        protective = await self._record_protective(signal, occ, qty, con_id, protective)
507	
508	        result = await self.ib.place(
509	            contract, side=side, qty=qty,
510	            order_ref=ostore.order_ref(signal.trader_id, order_id),
511	            order_type=order_type, limit_price=sent_limit,
512	            protective_exit=protective,
513	        )
514	        # Monotonic write: a fast push callback may already have advanced this row to
515	        # FILLED between place() returning and here — advance_order won't let the
516	        # immediate SUBMITTED clobber it.
517	        await ostore.advance_order(
518	            self.conn, order_id,
519	            status=result.status, filled_qty=result.filled_qty,
520	            avg_fill_price=result.avg_fill_price, broker_order_id=result.broker_order_id,
521	            broker_perm_id=result.broker_perm_id, error=result.error,
522	        )
523	        # An entry that's rejected/cancelled outright (no fill) never opens a position, so
524	        # its just-recorded protective legs have nothing to protect — settle them now.
525	        if result.status in (ostore.REJECTED, ostore.CANCELLED) and result.filled_qty == 0:
526	            await self._settle_orphaned_protective(signal.trader_id, signal.message_id)
527	        await self._notify_status(signal, result, order_id)
528	
529	    async def _settle_orphaned_protective(self, trader_id: str, message_id: int | None) -> None:
530	        """Cancel the working protective legs spawned by an entry that died without opening
531	        a position — at the broker (by ref; a no-op if a leg was never armed or is already
532	        gone) and in our books. Keyed by the entry's message, which its legs share."""
533	        for leg in await ostore.working_protective_for_message(self.conn, message_id):
534	            await self.ib.cancel(ostore.order_ref(trader_id, leg["order_id"]))
535	        await ostore.cancel_protective_for_message(self.conn, message_id)
536	
537	    async def _record_protective(
538	        self, signal, occ, qty, con_id, protective: ProtectiveExit | None,
539	    ) -> ProtectiveExit | None:
540	        """Create a PENDING SELL row for each protective leg and return a ProtectiveExit
541	        carrying those rows' order_refs (so the broker tags each leg). Returns None when
542	        there is nothing to protect — then the entry is placed plainly, as before."""
543	        if protective is None or not protective.has_any:
544	            return None
545	        stop_ref = take_profit_ref = ""
546	        if protective.take_profit_price is not None:
547	            tp_id = await ostore.create_order(
548	                self.conn, signal=signal, occ_symbol=occ, requested_qty=qty,
549	                limit_price=protective.take_profit_price, con_id=con_id,
550	                status=ostore.PENDING, signal_type="take_profit", side="SELL",
551	            )
552	            take_profit_ref = ostore.order_ref(signal.trader_id, tp_id)
553	        if protective.stop_price is not None:
554	            sl_id = await ostore.create_order(
555	                self.conn, signal=signal, occ_symbol=occ, requested_qty=qty,
556	                limit_price=protective.stop_price, con_id=con_id,
557	                status=ostore.PENDING, signal_type="stop_loss", side="SELL",
558	            )
559	            stop_ref = ostore.order_ref(signal.trader_id, sl_id)
560	        return ProtectiveExit(
561	            stop_price=protective.stop_price,
562	            take_profit_price=protective.take_profit_price,
563	            stop_ref=stop_ref, take_profit_ref=take_profit_ref,
564	        )
565	
566	    # ---- broker order-update reconciliation ----------------------------
567	    async def on_order_update(self, update) -> None:
568	        """Reconcile a broker-neutral OrderUpdate (entry late-fill, or a protective exit
569	        triggering/cancelling) back into the orders table and notify. Registered with the
570	        broker in main; keyed by the order_ref we assigned at placement. Idempotent and
571	        monotonic via advance_order, so duplicate/out-of-order callbacks are safe."""
572	        order_id = ostore.order_id_from_ref(update.order_ref)
573	        if not order_id:
574	            return
575	        row = await ostore.get_order(self.conn, order_id)
576	        if row is None:
577	            log.warning("order update for unknown ref %s", update.order_ref)
578	            return
579	        changed = await ostore.advance_order(
580	            self.conn, order_id,
581	            status=update.status, filled_qty=update.filled_qty,
582	            avg_fill_price=update.avg_fill_price, broker_order_id=update.broker_order_id,
583	            error=update.error,
584	        )
585	        if not changed:
586	            return  # stale or already-settled update; nothing new to surface
587	        # A protective leg that just filled closes the position — settle its OCA siblings
588	        # (mirror the broker's one-cancels-other so no stale PENDING leg lingers).
589	        if update.status == ostore.FILLED and row["signal_type"] in ostore.PROTECTIVE_TYPES:
590	            for sib in await ostore.protective_siblings(self.conn, row):
591	                await ostore.advance_order(self.conn, sib["order_id"], status=ostore.CANCELLED)
592	        # An entry that goes terminal without ever filling (cancelled in TWS, expired, or a
593	        # late reject) opened no position — settle its protective legs so they don't orphan.
594	        entry_filled = max(float(row["filled_qty"] or 0), float(update.filled_qty or 0))
595	        if (update.status in (ostore.CANCELLED, ostore.REJECTED)
596	                and row["signal_type"] == "buy" and entry_filled == 0):
597	            await self._settle_orphaned_protective(row["trader_id"], row["message_id"])
598	        await self._notify_order_update(row, update)
599	
600	    # ---- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
601	    async def _trader_exposure(self, trader_id: str) -> float:
602	        """Live mark-to-market exposure for a trader's *committed* contracts (× 100/contract):
603	        filled positions PLUS resting unfilled entry BUYs. Including the standing remainder
604	        means buys that haven't filled yet still consume exposure headroom, so a burst of
605	        buys can't collectively overshoot the per-trader cap. A filled position is valued at
606	        its live mark (falling back to entry premium); a standing order is valued worst-case
607	        at its limit price (the most it could cost), falling back to the live mark."""
608	        total = 0.0
609	        for p in await ostore.open_positions(self.conn, trader_id):
610	            px = await self._mark_or(
611	                p["ticker"], p["expiry"], p["option_type"], p["strike"],
612	                fallback=p["entry_premium"],
613	            )
614	            total += p["net_qty"] * px * MULTIPLIER
615	        for s in await ostore.standing_buy_orders(self.conn, trader_id):
616	            px = s["limit_price"]
617	            if px is None:  # market order (no limit): estimate from the live mark
618	                px = await self._mark_or(
619	                    s["ticker"], s["expiry"], s["option_type"], s["strike"], fallback=0.0,
620	                )
621	            total += s["remaining"] * px * MULTIPLIER
622	        return total
623	
624	    async def _mark_or(
625	        self, ticker: str, expiry: str, option_type: str, strike: float, *, fallback: float,
626	    ) -> float:
627	        """Best-available live mark for a contract, or `fallback` if it can't be priced.
628	        Valuation must never break sizing, so any error falls back too."""
629	        try:
630	            contract = build_option(
631	                ticker, date.fromisoformat(expiry), option_type, strike)
632	            if await self.ib.qualify(contract) is not None:
633	                px = await self.ib.mark(contract)
634	                if px:
635	                    return px
636	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - valuation must not break sizing
637	            pass
638	        return fallback
639	
640	    def _entry_limit(self, premium: float) -> float:
641	        return round(premium * (1 + self.config.policy.spread), 2)
642	
643	    def _exit_limit(self, premium: float) -> float:
644	        return round(premium * (1 - self.config.policy.spread), 2)
645	
646	    # ---- notification fan-out (no-op if notifier is None) --------------
647	    async def _notify_placed(self, signal, side, qty, limit_price, order_id) -> None:
648	        if self.notifier:
649	            await self.notifier.notify_placed(signal, side, qty, limit_price, order_id)

652	        if self.notifier:
653	            await self.notifier.notify_status(signal, result, order_id)
654	
655	    async def _notify_order_update(self, row: dict, update) -> None:

657	        kind (buy / take_profit / stop_loss / ...). Logs always; uses an optional notifier
658	        hook if one exists so the Notifier protocol stays minimal."""
659	        log.info(
660	            "Order update %s (%s %s): %s filled=%g",
661	            row["order_id"], row["signal_type"], row["occ_symbol"],
662	            update.status, update.filled_qty,
663	        )
664	        if self.notifier and hasattr(self.notifier, "notify_order_update"):

667	            if row["signal_type"] in ostore.PROTECTIVE_TYPES:
668	                parent = await ostore.entry_order_id_for(self.conn, row["message_id"])
669	                if parent:
670	                    row = {**row, "parent_order_id": parent}
671	            await self.notifier.notify_order_update(row, update)

674	        log.info("Skipped %s %s: %s", signal.trader_id, signal.trade.action, reason)
675	        if self.notifier:
676	            await self.notifier.notify_skip(signal, reason)

1	"""Order logic — the single place a developer tunes how orders behave.
2	
3	Everything here is **pure** (no broker, no IO) so it is exhaustively unit-testable,
4	exactly like [sizing.py](sizing.py) and [risk.py](risk.py). The executor and the
5	broker adapters read these values and helpers; they never hard-code order rules of
6	their own.
7	
8	`OrderPolicy` is the canonical, tunable block (loaded from the ``ORDER_POLICY`` section
9	of [config.json](../config.json) by [config.py](config.py)). It holds:
10	
11	* **Pricing / sizing knobs** (formerly the ``EXECUTION`` block): ``spread``,
12	  ``trim_fraction``, ``scale_up``, ``scale_down``.
13	* **Protective exits — stop loss & take profit** as a fraction of the entry premium:
14	  ``stop_loss_pct`` / ``take_profit_pct``. A per-trader override (on
15	  ``config.Trader``) takes precedence over these global defaults; ``None`` disables
16	  that leg.
17	
18	## Additional rules
19	
20	New order-logic rules belong here, as fields on ``OrderPolicy`` plus a pure helper —
21	so the whole surface a developer tunes stays in one module. Wire each new field through
22	``config.load_config`` and document it in
23	[order_processing.md](../order_processing.md).
24	"""
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	from dataclasses import dataclass
28	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
29	
30	if TYPE_CHECKING:  # avoid an import cycle (config imports OrderPolicy)
31	    from .config import Trader
32	
33	
34	@dataclass(frozen=True)
35	class OrderPolicy:
36	    spread: float = 0.05              # limit buffer: a priced order limits at premium ± spread
37	    trim_fraction: float = 0.5        # fraction of a holding a TRIM closes
38	    scale_up: float = 1.5             # qty multiplier for a SCALE_UP trade
39	    scale_down: float = 0.5           # qty multiplier for a SCALE_DOWN trade
40	    capital_fraction: float = 1.0     # global throttle: only deploy this fraction of the account (1.0 = all)
41	    # Protective exits, as a fraction of the entry premium. None disables that leg.
42	    stop_loss_pct: float | None = None      # e.g. 0.5 -> stop at premium * (1 - 0.5)
43	    take_profit_pct: float | None = None     # e.g. 1.0 -> target at premium * (1 + 1.0)
44	
45	
46	@dataclass(frozen=True)
47	class ProtectiveExit:
48	    """A stop loss and/or take profit to attach to an entry, in broker-neutral terms.
49	    Either price may be None (that leg is disabled). The executor fills in the two
50	    ``*_ref`` order references so the adapter can tag each protective leg and fills
51	    reconcile back to our rows by ref alone."""
52	    stop_price: float | None
53	    take_profit_price: float | None
54	    stop_ref: str = ""
55	    take_profit_ref: str = ""
56	
57	    @property
58	    def has_any(self) -> bool:
59	        return self.stop_price is not None or self.take_profit_price is not None
60	
61	
62	def stop_loss_price(entry_premium: float, pct: float | None) -> float | None:
63	    """Stop price `pct` below the entry premium (e.g. pct=0.5 -> 50% below). None/invalid
64	    inputs disable the leg. Floored at one cent so it stays a valid, positive price."""
65	    if pct is None or entry_premium is None or entry_premium <= 0 or pct <= 0:
66	        return None
67	    return round(max(0.01, entry_premium * (1 - pct)), 2)
68	
69	
70	def take_profit_price(entry_premium: float, pct: float | None) -> float | None:
71	    """Target price `pct` above the entry premium (e.g. pct=1.0 -> double). None/invalid
72	    inputs disable the leg."""
73	    if pct is None or entry_premium is None or entry_premium <= 0 or pct <= 0:
74	        return None
75	    return round(entry_premium * (1 + pct), 2)
76	
77	
78	def effective_sl_tp(
79	    policy: OrderPolicy, trader: "Trader | None"
80	) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
81	    """Resolve the (stop_loss_pct, take_profit_pct) in effect for a trade: a per-trader
82	    override wins over the global policy default; otherwise the global default applies."""
83	    sl = policy.stop_loss_pct
84	    tp = policy.take_profit_pct
85	    if trader is not None:
86	        if getattr(trader, "stop_loss_pct", None) is not None:
87	            sl = trader.stop_loss_pct
88	        if getattr(trader, "take_profit_pct", None) is not None:
89	            tp = trader.take_profit_pct
90	    return sl, tp
91	
92	
93	def protective_exit(
94	    entry_premium: float, policy: OrderPolicy, trader: "Trader | None"
95	) -> ProtectiveExit | None:
96	    """Build the protective exit for a BUY at `entry_premium`, applying the trader's
97	    SL/TP overrides over the global policy. Returns None when both legs are disabled
98	    (so the executor places a plain order, exactly as before)."""
99	    sl_pct, tp_pct = effective_sl_tp(policy, trader)
100	    stop = stop_loss_price(entry_premium, sl_pct)
101	    target = take_profit_price(entry_premium, tp_pct)
102	    if stop is None and target is None:
103	        return None
104	    return ProtectiveExit(stop_price=stop, take_profit_price=target)

I have completed a thorough analysis of the broker integration layer. Here are my findings.

---

# Broker Integration Layer: Failure Mode Analysis

Two show-stoppers first (one deterministic, one money-losing), then the systematic failure modes per your nine areas, then existing protections and the fix-planning shortlist. All paths are absolute.

## CRITICAL BUG #1 — Bot does not start (deterministic AttributeError)

- (a) What breaks: The process connects to the broker, then crashes constructing the `SafetySweeper`. The bot never begins trading.
- (b) Trigger: Every startup, unconditionally. The most recent commit `8dcce82` ("Added Order Timeout Feature") wired `buy_fill_timeout` through `main.py`, `safety.py`, and `config.json`, but never added the field to the `Safety` dataclass or its loader.
- (c) Evidence:
  - `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/main.py:108` reads `cfg.safety.buy_fill_timeout`.
  - `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/config.py:67-75` — `Safety` (frozen dataclass) defines only `enabled, interval, drift_epsilon, orphan_grace`. No `buy_fill_timeout`.
  - `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/config.py:180-185` — loader never reads `BUY_FILL_TIMEOUT`.
  - `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/config.json:33` has `"BUY_FILL_TIMEOUT": 600` — silently ignored.
  - Accessing a nonexistent attribute on a frozen dataclass raises `AttributeError`. Confirmed the working tree is clean at HEAD `8dcce82`, so this is the runnable state.
  - Not caught by tests: `tests/test_safety.py:66` constructs `SafetySweeper(...)` directly with an explicit `buy_fill_timeout=` kwarg, bypassing `cfg.safety` entirely; no test runs `amain()`.
- (d) Severity: stuck-state / total outage (bot down every launch).

## CRITICAL BUG #2 — Moomoo emulated OCA over-cancels via empty-string sentinel

- (a) What breaks: The `_watch` loop treats `oca == ""` (the "no group" sentinel) as a real OCA group key, so one fill cancels every other watched order that also has `oca == ""`.
- (b) Trigger scenarios:
  - Normal operation with two or more concurrent resting entries: entries are tracked with `oca=""`. When entry A fills, `_cancel_oca_siblings(A, "")` cancels every other pending entry (all share `oca==""`), across unrelated contracts/traders.
  - After any restart: `resync` re-tracks all non-terminal orders (entries AND protective legs) with `oca=""`. The next FILLED on any order then cancels every other working order account-wide.
- (c) Evidence:
  - `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/moomoo.py:249` — entry tracked `oca=""`.
  - `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/moomoo.py:376-377` — `_cancel_oca_siblings` is called on every `status == "FILLED"`.
  - `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/moomoo.py:381-386` — no guard for empty `oca`; matches on `info["oca"] == oca`.
  - `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/moomoo.py:442` — `resync` re-tracks non-terminal orders with `oca=""`.
- (d) Severity: money-losing (unwanted mass cancellation of live entries/exits) and stuck-state after restart. Note the executor's DB-side sibling settle (`executor.py:589-591`) only updates the books, not the broker, so on Moomoo this watch-loop path is the only thing that cancels the real survivor — and it over-fires.

---

## 1. Disconnect / reconnect

- No reconnection logic exists for either broker. A repo-wide search finds only `isConnected()` calls; no `disconnectedEvent`, watchdog, or reconnect. `resync()` runs once at startup only (`/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/main.py:103`), never on a mid-session reconnect.
- IBKR, order placed while socket is down: `self.ib.placeOrder(...)` at `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/ibkr.py:178` raises `ConnectionError`. It propagates through `place()` → `_place_and_record` → `process_message`, and is swallowed by the executor loop's blanket handler at `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/executor.py:123-124`. The order row was already inserted PENDING at `executor.py:498` (before the broker call), so the signal is effectively silently dropped and later CANCELLED by the orphan reaper after `orphan_grace` (`safety.py:60-69`). Trade missed. Severity: money-losing (missed entries/exits), self-healing state.
- IBKR callback re-registration: `orderStatusEvent += self._on_order_status` at `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/ibkr.py:95` runs inside `connect()`. There is no reconnect today, but if `connect()` is ever called twice, the handler double-registers (`+=`) and every update fires twice. Latent. Severity: cosmetic-to-stuck depending on future reconnect wiring.
- Moomoo `is_connected()` is a liveness lie: `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/moomoo.py:96-97` only checks `self._trd is not None and self._quote is not None`. If OpenD dies (its unit is `Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=5` — `deploy/opend.service:18-19`), the contexts remain non-None; `is_connected()` returns True and the dashboard's `account_provider` (`main.py:111-112`) reports connected while nothing works. Severity: stuck-state / misleading.
- Moomoo watch loop survives gateway *errors* but not *exceptions*: the poll guard `if ret == ft.RET_OK` (`moomoo.py:348`) tolerates OpenD returning error codes, but the loop body (`moomoo.py:341-357`) has no `try/except`, so if `order_list_query` raises (connection reset inside futu), the task dies. `_ensure_watch` only restarts it on the next `place()` (`moomoo.py:337-339`), so lifetime reconciliation and OCA emulation stop for all in-flight legs until then. Severity: money-losing (stops firing/cancelling stops) / stuck.
- Fills during downtime: recovered only by the startup `resync` on a full process restart, or by drift detection. Because there is no reconnect, a fill while merely disconnected (process alive) is not replayed until the process is restarted.

## 2. Moomoo emulated bracket (`_watch`) failure modes

- Crash while legs unarmed → position opens unprotected: the protective spec is stored in memory only at `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/moomoo.py:257` (`self._watched[order_id]["protective"] = ...`). If the process crashes after the entry is placed but before it fills, `resync` re-tracks the entry but cannot restore the protective spec (`moomoo.py:435-448` doesn't carry it). The entry then fills post-restart, `_reconcile` sees `info["protective"] is None` (`moomoo.py:373-375`), and the stop/target are never armed. The PENDING protective rows get orphan-reaped. Result: a real open position with no stop-loss and no alert. Severity: money-losing (HIGH).
- Protective submit errors are silently swallowed: `/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/moomoo.py:293-301` — `oid, _ = await self._submit(...)` discards the error; `_track(None, ...)` is a no-op (`moomoo.py:305`). A rejected stop-loss leaves the position unprotected with no OrderUpdate and no alert (the PENDING row is reaped after grace). Severity: money-losing (HIGH).
- Cancel-of-survivor can kill the loop: `_cancel_oca_siblings` calls `modify_order` via `to_thread` (`moomoo.py:384-386`) with no error handling; a raise propagates up through `_reconcile` into the unguarded `_watch` loop and kills reconciliation; the survivor leg stays live. Severity: money-losing / stuck.
- Polling gap double-exposure: `poll_interval=1.0s` (`moomoo.py:54,356`) means when one leg fills, its sibling can remain live for roughly a poll interval (longer under rate-limit throttling, see #9) before emulated cancel — a brief window where both a stop and target could execute. Severity: money-losing (bounded).
- Duplicate leg placement on restart is not the failure mode (resync does not re-place); the actual restart failure is the unarmed/unprotected case above, which is worse.

## 3. Order ID / ref mapping

- Refs are stable and collision-free across restarts: `order_ref = f"{trader_id}:{order_id}"` where `order_id` is a `uuid4().hex` (`/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/orders.py:28-30,54`). No post-restart collisions.
- IBKR reverse-map survives restart: in-memory `self._trades` is lost, but `_lookup_trade` falls back to scanning `ib.trades()` by `orderRef` (`/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/ibkr.py:187-197`). Good, provided the order is still in the client's open/completed set.
- Moomoo reverse-map: `_oid_for_ref` scans in-memory `_watched` (`moomoo.py:310-315`), rebuilt for non-terminal orders by `resync` via the `remark` field. Truncation risk: `remark=order_ref[:64]` (`moomoo.py:278`). A `trader_id` longer than 31 chars truncates the 32-char uuid tail; `order_id_from_ref` then returns a wrong/short id and the update lands on no row ("order update for unknown ref", `executor.py:577`). Severity: stuck/lost update, low-probability (depends on trader-id length).
- Update for an order placed before a restart: reconciles correctly because the uuid ref persists in the DB; `advance_order` no-ops if the row is already terminal (`orders.py:117`). Good.

## 4. place() / cancel() / modify() error handling

- IBKR untransmitted-parent trap: when protective children exist, `parent.transmit=False` (`/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/ibkr.py:176`) and only the last child transmits the group (`ibkr.py:245-256`). If `_attach_children` raises partway (e.g. a child `placeOrder` fails), the parent is left placed-but-never-transmitted at TWS while the exception propagates and the message is dropped. Severity: stuck-state (invisible resting parent).
- IBKR cancel/modify on a dead socket raise (`cancelOrder`/`placeOrder`, `ibkr.py:203,210,215`). In the executor exit path these are awaited without a local guard (`executor.py:432,473,478`), so a raise aborts the exit and drops the message. Severity: stuck (protective legs not resized/cancelled).
- Moomoo has no per-RPC timeout: only context creation is bounded by `wait_for` (`moomoo.py:83-87`). Every trading RPC (`place_order`, `order_list_query`, `accinfo_query`, `get_market_snapshot`) runs via bare `asyncio.to_thread`. If OpenD hangs, the await never returns and — because the executor is a single serial loop — all trading stalls indefinitely. Severity: stuck-state (HIGH).
- Partial failure (entry filled, protective rejected): IBKR surfaces the reject via `orderStatusEvent`; Moomoo silently drops it (see #2). 
- Clean paths that do work: Moomoo `_submit` maps `ret != RET_OK` to a proper REJECTED `PlaceResult` (`moomoo.py:283-284, 240-243`); IBKR `_result` maps status ladders including Inactive disambiguation (`ibkr.py:258-307`).

## 5. Market-data dependence (sizing off live mark)

- Well protected on the entry path: a price-less (market) buy sizes off `mark()`, and a `None`/`0` mark short-circuits to skip `no_mark` (`/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/executor.py:277-281`). IBKR `mark()` returns None unless a value is `> 0` (`ibkr.py:151-155`); Moomoo `extract_mark` requires `> 0` (`moomoo_codec.py:46-64`). NaN/None/zero are all handled.
- Stale-mark mispricing: both accept `close` / `prev_close_price` as a valid mark (`ibkr.py:151`, `moomoo_codec.py:60`). With market closed (and default `market_data_type=3` delayed, `config.py:53`), a market buy can size off yesterday's close. Severity: money-losing (mispricing, not a crash).
- Exposure understatement: `_trader_exposure` values positions via `_mark_or`, which falls back to `entry_premium` or `0.0` on any failure (`executor.py:601-638`). Stale/failed marks understate exposure and can let the per-trader cap be exceeded. Severity: low-med.
- Qualification: `qualify() is None` → skip `qualify_failed` (`executor.py:271,405`). Moomoo qualify is authoritative against the live chain (`moomoo.py:149-188`); IBKR ambiguity leaves `conId==0` → None (`ibkr.py:141-143`). Handled.

## 6. Moomoo codec symbol translation edges

- `to_moomoo_code` = `US.{TICKER}{YYMMDD}{C|P}{strike*1000, zfill 6}` (`/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/brokers/moomoo_codec.py:13-23`).
- Weeklies / non-standard expiries: fine (date-driven).
- Index options: `_underlying_code` hard-codes the `US.` prefix (`moomoo.py:136`), so index underlyings (SPX/SPXW/NDX) likely won't resolve on the chain → `qualify` returns None → contract simply won't trade on Moomoo. Functional gap, not a mispricing (qualify is authoritative). Severity: functional/cosmetic.
- High strikes (≥ 1000): `strike*1000` exceeds 6 digits; `zfill(6)` only pads, so the hand-built code widens. This only affects the pre-qualify fallback in `mark()`/`place()`; since the executor always qualifies first and caches `row["code"]`, the authoritative code is used. Severity: low.

## 7. OrderUpdate delivery semantics

- IBKR: push, at-least-once, de-duplicated by `_last_status` (`ibkr.py:107-109`). Concurrency hazard: `_on_order_status` schedules each update with `asyncio.ensure_future(self._dispatch(...))` (`ibkr.py:118`), so multiple updates for the same order can interleave inside `advance_order`'s non-atomic read-modify-write (`orders.py:116-140`), racing `filled_qty`/status. Low-med probability, could corrupt filled quantity. Moomoo reconciles sequentially in the watch loop, so it does not have this race.
- Recovery breadth: `resync` replays current states at startup only (`ibkr.py:309-330`, `moomoo.py:426-449`). `executions()` is defined on both adapters (`ibkr.py:358-359`, `moomoo.py:462-468`) but is never called anywhere — there is no `reqExecutions`/fill-history replay. 
- Moomoo has no position backstop: `positions()` returns `occ_symbol=None` (`moomoo.py:451-460`), and the drift pass skips when nothing is occ-keyed (`safety.py:130-134`). So a Moomoo fill missed by a dead watch task — or a GTC leg that aged out of `order_list_query`'s default same-day window before a later-day restart — is never reconciled and the books stay permanently wrong. Severity: med-high (Moomoo-specific).

## 8. Trading-hours / paper-vs-live / currency

- RTH: IBKR entries are DAY, protective legs GTC (`ibkr.py:217,255`); `outsideRth` is not set (RTH-only). Pre-open orders return Inactive-without-error and are deliberately kept SUBMITTED so they (and their legs) are not orphaned (`ibkr.py:269-274`, tested in `tests/test_ibkr_status.py`). Handled well.
- No paper-vs-live guard for IBKR: safety depends entirely on `IB_PORT` (`config.py:48-53`); the docstring says paper (`ibkr.py:4-6`) but nothing enforces it. Point it at a live port and it trades live. Severity: operational (med).
- Moomoo: defaults to SIMULATE; REAL additionally needs `unlock_trade`, explicitly out of scope (`moomoo.py:9-11,57`), so a REAL `place_order` fails → REJECTED. Safe-by-default but means live Moomoo is non-functional. `check_moomoo` adds an explicit `--allow-real` guard (`check_moomoo.py:103`); the main flow has none but is protected by the unlock failure.
- Currency: USD assumed throughout (`options.py:35`; IBKR account values prefer USD/BASE, `ibkr.py:52-58`). Low risk for US options.

## 9. Rate limits / pacing

- Moomoo order-poll pacing: the watch loop polls `order_list_query` every `poll_interval=1.0s` (`moomoo.py:54,356`) — about 30 calls/30s, well over futu's order-query pacing (order-list endpoints are roughly 10/30s). Under load this throttles; the loop reads throttled responses as "no data" (`moomoo.py:348`), delaying reconciliation and OCA cancellation and widening the double-exposure window from #2/#4. Severity: money-losing/stuck (HIGH for Moomoo).
- Per-buy market-data bursts: `_trader_exposure` marks every open position and every standing order and qualifies on every buy (`executor.py:601-638`). On Moomoo this fans out to `get_market_snapshot`/`get_option_chain` (chain limit ~10/30s); on IBKR to `reqTickers`/`reqContractDetails` (IB pacing ~50 msg/s plus soft contract-details limits). No caching or throttling of qualify/mark. Severity: med (IBKR), med-high (Moomoo).

## Existing protections worth preserving

- Monotonic, idempotent single write path `advance_order` — terminal never regresses, `filled_qty` only grows, stale lower-rank statuses can't clobber (`/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/orders.py:101-141`). This is what makes duplicate/out-of-order callbacks safe.
- Startup recovery via `resync` on both adapters, wired in `main.py:103` (`ibkr.py:309-330` also pulls completed orders; `moomoo.py:426-449` re-tracks non-terminal orders).
- Safety sweeper (`/home/krubics/LocalProjects/Clarence/only_trades/safety.py`): orphan reap of never-placed PENDING rows (`:60-69`), stale-BUY timeout that cancels the entry and settles its legs (`:72-109`), expiry sweep (`:112-125`), and position-drift detection with a conservative single-holder startup auto-settle (`:128-165`). Passes are individually wrapped by `_safe` (`:53-57`).
- Callback isolation: `_dispatch`/`_emit` swallow callback exceptions so a bad reconciler can't kill the event loop/watch loop (`ibkr.py:120-124`, `moomoo.py:388-394`); the executor and sweeper loops likewise wrap each iteration (`executor.py:122-126`).

- Oversell guard `has_working_exit` (`orders.py:234-248`) and the committed-contracts overbuy gate (`orders.py:333-342`).
- Moomoo defers protective legs until the entry actually opens, avoiding resting SELLs against a nonexistent position (`moomoo.py:254-257,373-375`).
- `_settle_orphaned_protective` cleans up legs when an entry dies without filling, both at placement and via callback (`executor.py:525-535,594-597`).
